charts.title: molecular-turing-pattern-movie
charts.caption: Animated GIF of the flagship chemical-channel run: a near-uniform Gray-Scott seed on a 128x128 periodic field (u~=1, v~=0 plus small noise and a few nucleation patches) destabilizes under the canonical differential-diffusion regime (Du=0.16, Dv=0.08) into an emergent finite-amplitude, nucleation-driven Gray-Scott spot pattern (not linear-instability Turing sensu stricto) -- the molecular interface's chemical channel (§Molecular interface, Fig 6) made spatial: local autocatalytic reactions plus differential diffusion producing emergent spatial structure. Re-baked over the same run cited in this study's behavior tests, for provenance.

charts.title: molecular-thermal-graded-movie
charts.caption: Animated GIF of the thermal-channel run: the IDENTICAL chemistry, diffusion, and seed as the flagship, plus a raised uniform temperature field (T=1.2) Arrhenius-scaling the reaction (Ea=0.15). The pattern GRADES -- coarsening to fewer, larger domains (~12 -> ~2) while staying patterned rather than collapsing. Watch it beside the flagship GIF: the temperature field is a static rate multiplier (no heat transport, no reaction->heat feedback) -- a temperature parameter modulating the chemical channel, not a chemistry collapse and not a second physically-transported channel. Re-baked over the run cited in this study's behavior tests.

charts.title: molecular-metrics
charts.caption: Interactive Plotly panel of the flagship run, synced to the GIF's time axis: the inhibitor-field spatial variance v_var (the primary pattern-formation metric, rising from ~0.0011 toward the patterned plateau ~0.0119) plotted with the connected-domain count n_domains (~12 spots). Together the two traces are the load-bearing evidence that the chemical channel genuinely patterns -- emergent variance and discrete domains, not a uniform relaxation. Interactive: hover for exact per-tick values.
